daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo met with UN Secretary General at his private residence in Hambalang, with Guterres staying overnight at the location. The UN chief praised Indonesia's contribution to global peacekeeping efforts. Former Foreign Minister Retno Marsudi attended the meeting at Hambalang.

  • The Prabowo-Gibran administration has completed its first two years with Rp225 trillion worth of downstreaming projects across various sectors.
  • The administration announced it has halted rice imports for domestic use under the current government's food security policy.
  • Former President Jokowi sent birthday greetings to President Prabowo on his 75th birthday.
  • A former member of the 2019-2024 DPR Commission II stated that the PKPU article which allowed Gibran to qualify for candidacy was never discussed during their tenure.
  • The KPK conducted two OTT operations in one week, exposing alleged corruption involving BNPB disaster funds and bribery involving the Klaten regent.
  • The Constitutional Court issued a two-year deadline for military court reform, making judicial reform increasingly urgent.
  • An observer said the Constitutional Court ruling is expected to end arbitrary actions by security forces against civilians.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Vice President Gibran, accompanied by East Java Governor Khofifah, visited Polygon bicycle factory and expressed pride in Indonesia's bicycle export achievements. Japan's Defense Minister praised JSDF personnel who participated in firefighting efforts in Indonesia. Two Indonesian researchers received Indroyono Soesilo Awards in India for their contributions.

  • Indonesia's Deputy Defense Minister stressed the need for faster post-disaster recovery mechanisms.
  • The Trade Ministry is promoting ASEAN trade deals to boost Indonesian exports across the region.
  • Indonesia is seeking European partnerships in tilapia and seaweed sectors to expand export markets.
  • The Indonesian Embassy in Paris urged Indonesian citizens to increase vigilance amid protest waves in France.

Other

The Indonesia Stock Exchange lowered the auto-rejection boundary for stocks to 7 percent starting today, a significant change in trading rules. The government is turning to the digital economy to achieve a 6 percent growth target in 2027. The Prabowo-Gibran administration has activated 10,070 village cooperatives across Indonesia.

  • The government's three million homes program has reached 324,213 units in construction and completion.
  • Eleven downstreaming projects in North Maluku could absorb 10,000 workers when fully operational.
  • MUI called on law enforcement to prosecute forest fire perpetrators without exception amid continuing forest fires.
  • BRIN is studying the effectiveness of dry ice for tackling forest fire smoke pollution.
  • A DPR member requested that former forest fire areas be planted with hardwood trees rather than oil palm.

weekly_review.html:
The Constitutional Court found no proof of Vice President Gibran's high school diploma but declined to disqualify him, leaving the matter to parliament.

On October 6, the Constitutional Court ruled that petitioners lacked standing to challenge Gibran Rakabuming Raka's educational qualifications, but in its reasoning the court stated it found no convincing evidence of a high school-equivalent diploma for the vice president. The decision triggered calls from PDIP politicians for the House of Representatives to exercise its constitutional authority through an inquiry or impeachment motion. By mid-week, Commission II announced it was studying the ruling and would consider the matter during deliberations on electoral law reform. On Friday, former President Jokowi dismissed the controversy as a political operation designed to damage his and Gibran's reputations, claiming "free riders" had exploited the issue. By Sunday, analysts noted the House faced a constitutional dilemma: the ball now sits with the legislature, which could pursue impeachment but appears reluctant given the political will required.

President Prabowo conducted three major reshuffles in October, culminating in a swap between army chief Maruli Simanjuntak and deputy TNI commander Tandyo Budi Revita.

After reshuffling 16 cabinet positions on October 1—including elevating Arrmanatha Nasir to foreign minister and Sugiono to coordinating minister—Prabowo carried out a second round on October 2 appointing 26 presidential advisers. On October 15, he executed his third reshuffle of the month, swapping the positions of General Maruli Simanjuntak and General Tandyo Budi Revita: Maruli moved from army chief to deputy TNI commander while Tandyo took over as head of the army. The formal handover ceremony took place the following day at TNI headquarters. Observers questioned what Prabowo was pursuing with three rounds of appointments in two weeks as the administration neared its two-year mark. On Saturday evening, the president summoned his full cabinet to Bogor Palace—not for a policy meeting but to host a banquet for visiting Russian Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov, introducing his ministerial team to the Russian delegation.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres arrived in Indonesia for a three-day visit to strengthen multilateral cooperation and honor Indonesian peacekeepers.

Guterres landed on Saturday, October 17, for what marks the first visit by a UN chief during Prabowo Subianto's presidency. His itinerary included meetings to discuss cooperation within the multilateral system and a planned visit to the TNI Peacekeeping Mission Center in Bogor, where he would lay a wreath honoring 50 fallen Indonesian peacekeepers and meet troops deploying to the Central African Republic. On Sunday, Prabowo received Guterres at his Hambalang residence, where the secretary-general praised Indonesia's foreign policy leadership and support for Palestine. The visit holds particular significance: Guterres is set to step down in December 2026, making this among his final official trips. He was scheduled to deliver a speech titled "Eight Decades of the United Nations: What Comes Next?" at the Foreign Ministry on Monday before returning to New York.

commentary_review.html:
Writing in Indonesia at Melbourne, Ary Hermawan argues that President Prabowo's sweeping October 2026 cabinet reshuffle signals preparation for a 2029 election showdown against Jokowi dynasty, despite both leaders publicly downplaying any rivalry. The most consequential move was replacing National Police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo, a close Jokowi ally who controlled what is described as Jokowi's 'brown army', with Gen. Suyudi Aryo Seto. This reshuffle appears designed to consolidate power and undermine Jokowi's loyalists ahead of the next presidential contest, suggesting their alliance has deteriorated significantly.

Writing in The Diplomat, Trystanto Sanjaya argues that while career diplomat Arrmanatha Nasir is highly qualified to restore Indonesia's foreign policy to a steadier course, his success hinges on whether he gains sufficient access to President Prabowo. Under predecessor Sugiono's tenure, Indonesian diplomats complained about chaotic workflow and being excluded from vital decisions made within Prabowo's inner circle, including controversial moves like endorsing a joint statement with China and joining BRICS. Reports indicate that even ministers face heavily curated and limited presidential access, which has handicapped coordination across governmental affairs including foreign policy.
